key_insight: CircuitATLAS uses a large, provenance-grounded neuroscience knowledge graph and agentic reasoning to find actionable circuit control points that can restore dysfunctional brain circuits, even when those molecules are not the primary disease-causing genes or proteins.
clinical_relevance: This approach could help prioritize therapeutic targets for neurological diseases by linking measurable circuit phenotypes to tractable molecular interventions and experimental validation.
method: Built a systems-neuroscience knowledge graph spanning diseases, phenotypes, circuits, cell types, regions, and molecular effectors while excluding direct disease-gene/protein shortcut edges.
Added 3.83 million nodes and 7.66 million edges, including 5.31 million LLM-extracted relations plus structured datasets and new in vivo measurements.
Used an agentic, lab-in-the-loop workflow to move from phenotype to target nomination, then validated ATP1A3 in vivo and advanced it into a structure-guided small-molecule campaign.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a very large graph (3.83M nodes, 7.66M edges) and a validation example in which ATP1A3 nomination was supported by in vivo 4-aminopyridine challenge experiments and downstream assay development.
watch_item: Performance depends on literature quality, graph curation, and experimental follow-up, so the framework may be sensitive to missing biology or bias in LLM-extracted relations.
paper_title: CircuitATLAS: Agentic reasoning over a systems neuroscience knowledge graph for target discovery in circuitopathies
